Every time Caya packs for a trip, he runs into the same problem: iPhone, iPad, MacBook, Vision Pro… does he actually need all of them?

Apple spent decades building distinct product categories around what each device could and couldn't do. But Apple Silicon changed that. Today, the hardware inside an iPad and a MacBook is increasingly similar—yet Apple still wants us to buy both. :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}

So in this episode, we look at Apple's $8,000 illusion of choice: how the iPhone killed the iPod, why the iPad never replaced the MacBook, what happened with the Vision Pro, and
title: every Apple device is the same device...
